reason: Value/transfer lens: the realistic public gain is about +0.000 (range -0.002..+0.001), not the claimed central +0.0008. It is below the +0.002 gate and well inside the 0.003 LB noise. (1) Ceiling: 424+28 = 452 FN out of a J union of 122,151+6,846+6,732 = 135,729 gives +0.0033. I confirmed this in fn_anatomy_exp39.md l.56, but it was measured on exp39, which has no readmit or gap filler. x138 already readmits 1,337/121,777 = 1.1% nodes on the dummy clips (CONTEXT L1515), so part of the pool is taken. Readmit is one round, so each open end gains at most one node. (2) The reachable pool is about 90% 6bba (a_never 1,740 of 1,907). There the misses are density misses, and a pretrained SimView UNet plus a simple watershed is out of domain (no preprocessing or scale script ships; README = torch.jit.load only). The 44b6 under-segmentation story covers only 167 a_never. (3) New FP channel. External candidates are not NMS'd against primary nodes. The same nucleus seen by the two detectors differs by a median of 1.46 um (92.5% <4 um, r2_critic.notes l.19), so about 20-27% of twins fall in the 2-4 um band. That band passes both the 2 um exclusion and the 4 um readmit radius. At the ~1,400 lab sites where p_u is a free end but the GT successor is already matched to another track (b_v_taken 701 + mirror b_u_diverted 706), the edge p_u->twin is an official FP (metrics.md l.21-30). At q ~0.1 that is ~140 FP, about -0.001. (4) Node multiplier: readmits happen at every open end (~5% of nodes interior ends/starts x 0.3-0.5 candidate hit) = ~1-2.5% nodes, which costs -0.0009 per 1%. The per-readmit algebra (benefit p/N vs cost 0.1/N) says the break-even TP yield is 10%, so this is second order to (3). Net: gross +0.0005..+0.0011, minus duplicate FP 0.0005..0.001, minus nodes 0.0005..0.0015. (5) Transfer: 44b6 is the dorado recording, whose public tracks were made with unet-simview itself. 44b6 lab numbers are therefore in-domain or possibly in-train for simview, and they are also only ~11 independent leak groups. Only 6bba is a fair judge. The detector is weaker on unseen test embryos, which scales both the gross gain and the duplicate or node costs, so the sign does not improve. (6) The added full-resolution 3D UNet pass (~1-2 h est.) pushes x138 toward its 27,000 s REPAIR_DEADLINE guard. That guard switches off the tail on the last movies, a downside that hits public and private alike.
fix_if_any: Make external candidates strictly additive to genuinely missing nuclei. (a) Exclude any simview candidate within 4.0 um (not 2) of any node at t: this is the r2 'no pred within 4 um' population that moved match<=7 from 0.988 to 0.998, and it removes the twin/duplicate FP channel. (b) Require simview support in 2 consecutive frames (t and t+1 within 3 um after the flow shift) so that one-frame watershed fragments are dropped. (c) Hard cap external readmits at <= 0.5% of nodes per movie, ranked by simview foreground mass. (d) No readmit next to a track start whose parent is within 10 um (protects forks and the 0.1 x division J). (e) Judge on 6bba only (SELECTION 6bba odd, CONFIRMATION 6bba even) with the gate >= +0.0015, CI90 > 0, node ratio <= +0.5%. Do not use 44b6 as evidence. (f) Budget runtime: (1,2,2) downsample plus fp16, and measure it against the 27,000 s guard on the dummy run. Even repaired, expect about +0.0003..+0.001 public, so it is only worth doing as a rider bundled with a larger change or as the validation step for a simview-based idea.
realistic_public_gain: -0.002 .. +0.001, central ~+0.0002 (idea's central +0.0008 is optimistic: it ignores x138's existing 1.1% readmit share and the 2-4 um duplicate FP channel)
realistic_private_gain: -0.002 .. +0.001, central ~+0.0001 (hidden embryos are 6bba-like and out of domain for simview; the runtime-guard downside applies here too)
